items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: this one came out real good and it's a good shot of the late Johnny Wig's and his group.

ctx.x: I see a photograph here of Johnny Wig's band that you took yourself. You like to take photographs?

Well, every... Once in a while? I don't get out to the Jazz Festival every year, but I try to get out when I can get out there. And when I do, I usually bring my camera. And as you know, at the Jazz Festival, which is held every year out at the fairgrounds here in New Orleans, there's about eight or ten different stages. And there's bands that are swapping around about every hour on all the various stages. And you get quite a variety of music, you've got Dixieland jazz and country and western and what have you.…
Did you ever play the festival? No, I never did.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I remember when he had that examination and everything. It just sounded hopeless from what Johnny Wiggs told me. Johnny I think was the one who told me about it.

ctx.x: What I like about Connie Jones is not only his marvelous playing, but like you just mentioned, he plays a lot of tunes, good old Dixieland tunes, that a lot of the other Dixieland bands don't play. Oh yeah. And that's what I enjoyed the year working with Sharky's Dixieland band, with the old Sharky's Kings of Dixieland. I enjoyed that year with Sharky because Sharky played a lot of good old Dixieland tunes that I had not played with any of the other groups. Even when I was with Al Hurd or the late George Arrod,…
I remember when he had that examination and everything. It just sounded hopeless from what Johnny Wiggs told me. Johnny I think was the one who told me about it. It was a shock.

Because, you know, George was so full of life. Oh, he was tremendous. Tremendous. I couldn't wait to get to work at night. I was getting three hours sleep a night in those days. Because in those days we were at the night shift. We would work nine or three and we'd be alternating with the Dukes of Dixieland or some other group like that or with Santa or some group, I don't recall. But at nine or three I'd get home at 315 or 320 and I had to get up at six and go to work to get ready to go to work because I had to…
